top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice clock is a new mechanism, independently reproduced and surpassed in several laboratories at 10^-18, with real reach into fundamental physics (redshift over millimetres, limits on drifting constants). The allocation to Katori (proposal and first demonstration) and Ye (accuracy and many-body regime) is the cleanest on the shortlist and every member who named laureates named exactly these two. A citation centred on magic-wavelength trapping separates it from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. An award is preferable to no award.
